card: Startup cost of warrior A: remove redundant instructions (e.g. `and dx,0 / or dx,0FFBh` -> direct mov, the jmp to the next line, the dead zombie_entry/zombie_scan block) and measure whether earlier entry into the replicator helps. Keep zom20a capture semantics.

Startup cost of warrior B: shorten/reorder B's initializer (cell writes, INT87 placement, quantizer) so the replicator starts earlier, without breaking zombie_entry (which reuses B code and the get_ip arithmetic).
Timing of A's zom20a capture: move A's INT87 earlier or later relative to the cell copy; check the race against competitors who also target zom20a; screen.
First-generation geometry: A gap 100h / B gap 600h and first copy CX values; try a few principled alternatives (e.g. equalize first-generation length).
A/B start synchronization: adjust startup lengths so A and B enter steady state in a controlled phase relation; measure partner interference.
Template copy counts: CX 9 vs 8 for first and later rebuilds in A and B (B uses CX 8 in its first copy). Verify mechanically (extra/short copied bytes) then screen.
A's step/stack motion (BP 4400h / DX 4000h): evaluate alternatives that keep full 64-position coverage (gcd with 10000h = 400h) and trail length 400h.
B's step (BP 2C00h / DX 2400h) vs V4's 2800h/2000h (only 32 positions) vs other full-coverage steps; V4 differs from V6 only here.
Band phases: A phase 2Ch, B phase 10h, zombie phases 2000h/3400h (added to AX); explore separations that minimize A/B/zombie lane overlap.
Quantization: divisor 3Ch on the load high byte; try other band schemes (different divisor, mask) that spread A, B and zombies better.

Lattice undercut: FAR_SEG 0FFBh (in-page 52h). Test 0FFAh (42h) / 0FF9h (32h) for BOTH warriors and captured zombies (all streams same lattice). Known: 10h below a crowd wins vs that crowd; check the cost on the plain field.
Separate lattice for captured zombies only (they run B's phoenix code) - can zombies live on an offset lattice without crossfire on A/B? Measure.
Captured zombies' motion: they run B's phoenix (DX 2400h, BP 2C00h, gap 600h). Give zombies their own step/gap tuned for speed-2 processes.
A/B lockstep separation: same step for A and B with a fixed relative offset (e.g. 8000h) using team-shared memory to coordinate the band; measure partner collisions and score.
Trail length per generation (BP-DX=400h): test 300h/500h/800h variants (keep coverage), considering anchor dwell exposure vs rebuild overhead.
Stack/anchor alignment: verify SP and anchor residues for all streams (A, B, zombies) and test whether any stream currently misaligns (rebuild failures).
Anchor encoding: `FF 1F` call far [bx] vs `FF 18` [bx+si] vs `FF 1C` [si] etc. - effect of which ModRM byte opponents' writes turn benign/fatal; measure.
Anchor redundancy: write a recovery word after the anchor (e.g. a second `FF 1F`) so common single-byte ModRM hits (FF CC = dec sp) fall through into a valid call; check rebuild still works.
Worker shortening: fewer instructions in the 18-byte worker (e.g. LES DI,[BX], keep CX, avoid XOR SI) to cut rebuild exposure; verify template/copy-count consistency.
Worker instruction order: reorder dependency-safe worker instructions to shrink the exposed window during rebuild; measure.

Kill pattern of our trail: the pushed CS word is FB 0F (STI; invalid). Explore FAR_SEG values whose low byte is immediately fatal (F6/F7 /1 are invalid in v6) while keeping a sane lattice; measure lethality vs cost.
Private memory layout: template at SS:0, cells 2C0h/280h; check whether cell/template positions interact with REP copy overrun (CX words copied beyond the template) and fix if harmful.
Rebuild exposure: the anchor+1..+22 window; try placing or splitting the worker to reduce overlap with incoming trails; prototype carefully.
Remove A's dead hunter code and use freed bytes for something useful (e.g. anchor recovery or a decoy) - measure each separately.
INT 86h for A/B (currently unused, 2 charges each): where could 256-byte bombs help without self-damage (e.g. ahead of own first trail, around zombie positions)? Prototype, screen.
INT 86h by captured zombies (each has 2 charges): use them at capture time (a zombie knows its own code location) to wipe something useful; screen.
zrl03-style two-step b/d capture without planting decoys: make B's first search kill the top decoy and the second capture the live tail, using V6's cell layout; check vs zombie competitors.
Fallback counter-bomb of the captured b/d zombie: `0E 07 0E 17` -> CC. Measure alternative 4-byte targets present in many 2025/2024 initializers (scan the binaries) and pick by field data.
NRG economics: any place where NRG (9B 9B) pays off (startup? zombies? worker?) given decay 1 per 5 rounds; prototype at most one well-reasoned variant.
INT 87h smart-bomb aimed at MOVSW-family anchors or workers (e.g. their rebuild template bytes) using a spare charge; verify target bytes in the binaries first.
Defensive INT 86h: overwrite our own abandoned initializer to remove signatures, or bomb regions opponents use to locate us; measure.
zom20c capture: its live loop is the 3rd of 8 identical copies (a forward search hits copies 0,1,2). Is there any charge budget/pattern that captures it? Prototype if feasible.
Capture the second (lower) zom20b/d: compute the charge budget (A, B, zom20a, b/d = 4 charges); try a reassignment that yields an extra capture without losing the counter-bomb.
Captured-process roles: all captured zombies become replicators. Try giving one captured zombie a different role (e.g. revive the trail hunter only for zombies, or a bomber) and measure.
Lane separation for captured zombies (speed 2 laps survivors): choose zombie phases/steps that minimize their crossings of A/B anchors; verify with a trace.
Make zom20a capture happen earlier (it depends on A's INT87 timing and on [4A17h] being written by B); measure capture rate (trace) and score.
Hook cell robustness: [4A17h] is a fixed shared cell (the V4/V6 family uses it too). Try a less collision-prone cell or a double-pointer scheme; measure vs lead_V6/lead_V4 threats.
zom20a capture robustness vs mimics: E2 F2 81 C3 also appears in Grindo/callfart/AnotherBit. Can a more specific pattern or search start avoid mimics? Measure vs zomb_* threats.
b/d capture search parameters: start DI, direction, pattern choice; measure capture rate and score vs zombie competitors.
Use leaked zombie information (zom20b/d write fixed addresses x612h/x226h; zom20c's column) to locate zombies precisely; prototype a direct-write capture if feasible.
Measure A/B partner trail collisions in the base (trace) and test a separation fix.
Captured zombies vs partners: do zombie trails kill A/B anchors or workers? Trace and fix (family/lattice consistency).
Team-shared memory communication: B reads A's band (or vice versa) to pick a complementary lane; prototype a minimal protocol.
Self-harm at startup: own writes ([4A17h], [5D13h], [9769h], INT87 replacements, stosw) hitting own or partner code; check with a trace and fix.
Pointer cell vs stack: verify no SP/stack interaction can corrupt the private pointer cells or the template in any stream (zombies have their own SS).

Hybrid pair: one warrior from zchain4 (strong on the plain 2025 field) + one from the base (robust vs leaders). Check family/lattice compatibility (zchain4 is also on lattice 52h, FAR_SEG 0FFBh) and zombie-cell interplay; screen.
Graft zchain4's zombie-chain idea (captured b/d captures zom20a with 41 93 E2 F2) into the base's charge budget if it frees a charge for another use; screen.
Graft combo_zrl03 ideas (decoy-immune capture pattern 0F EB F9 CC with the CC-high-byte cell trick) into the base without planting decoys; screen and threat-test vs lead_V6.
Independent idea of your choice inside the current architecture - justify it with engine facts and prior data, prototype, screen.
Radical new strategy family (not a far-call replicator tweak) prototyped quickly; screen once; report honestly even if it loses.
